first_impression.reaction: Our daughter sent this because she's nervous about saying vows in front of everyone. It's a gentle, well-mannered read with no silly slang, and the examples are lovely. I liked that it explains the legal words properly, with the actual Act. The vows are their business, not mine, so there's little here about money or who's responsible, but it's written with care and nothing made me wince. The legal quotes are a bit heavy on the iPad.

journey.quote: Many would rather say something true, say it well and hand the moment back to the ceremony.
journey.reaction: Hear, hear. Some of the vows I've sat through went on far too long. Sensible start.

journey.section: How long should short wedding vows be?
journey.quote: Read your vows aloud at the pace you would use in front of guests, with pauses, and time yourself on your phone.
journey.reaction: Practical. That's exactly what I'll tell her to do at the kitchen table.

journey.section: What words do you legally have to say when you marry in Australia?
journey.quote: When your celebrant is not a minister of religion, it is sufficient for each of you to say to the other, in the presence of the celebrant and the witnesses, the words set out in section 45(2) of the Marriage Act 1961:
journey.reaction: Good, they've gone to the actual law rather than guessing. That reassures me they take the legal side seriously.

journey.section: What words do you legally have to say when you marry in Australia?
journey.quote: Before the marriage is solemnised, a celebrant who is not a minister of religion of a recognised denomination says these words to you, in the presence of the witnesses, under section 46(1) of the Act:
journey.reaction: Two long legal quotes back to back. I read them, but it's dense on a small screen. A one-line plain summary underneath would help.

journey.quote: If you marry legally in another country, the legal wording follows that country.
journey.reaction: Useful to know. But if they marry in Italy, is the ceremony in Italian, and who checks the paperwork is right?

journey.quote: Through Wedded Concierge, one Wedded Advisor plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments with you, anywhere in the world, as your single point of contact.
journey.reaction: Payments is the word I was looking for. One person handling it is good. I'd want to know how those payments and deposits are protected.

journey.quote: Not only today, with everyone dressed up and the light just right, but the Tuesday nights, the airport queues and the years our hair turns grey.
journey.reaction: That one made me smile. That's what marriage actually is. I'll send that one to her.

journey.quote: I love you. Let's do this.
journey.reaction: A bit casual for a wedding to my ear, but I suppose that's the young ones. It's their choice.

journey.section: How do you say your vows with confidence?
journey.quote: Write your vows on a small, sturdy card in large print.
journey.reaction: Large print. Thank you. Someone who's actually stood up with shaking hands wrote this.

journey.section: How do you say your vows with confidence?
journey.quote: Ask your venue whether a microphone is available for the ceremony, who sets it up, and whether you can test it at the rehearsal.
journey.reaction: Yes. My mother is hard of hearing and would miss every word on a windy terrace. 'Who sets it up' is the right question, though I'd rather the Advisor asked it than my daughter.

journey.section: Saying it in your own words
journey.quote: Where you say them, and who flies in to hear them, is where a Wedded Advisor comes in.
journey.reaction: Fine, gently put. 'Who flies in' means Mum and her walking frame, and nothing here tells me how older guests are looked after.

unanswered_questions: If they marry overseas, who makes sure the legal paperwork and wording are right, and is the ceremony in English? (deferred business detail)
How are payments and deposits handled when the Wedded Advisor manages them, and are they protected? (deferred business detail)
Are fees quoted in AUD and agreed in writing? (deferred business detail)
Does the Wedded Advisor arrange things like a microphone and seating for older or hard-of-hearing guests at the ceremony? (deferred business detail)
Is the first conversation a phone call with a named person, and can I take part as a parent paying half?

turn_offs_found.quote: Through Wedded Concierge, one Wedded Advisor plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments with you, anywhere in the world, as your single point of contact.
turn_offs_found.why: It mentions payments but says nothing about deposits, contracts or who is accountable if a supplier lets us down. For a vows page that's forgivable, but it's the question I'd forward to my husband.

turn_offs_found.quote: "I call upon the persons here present to witness that I, A.B. (or C.D.), take thee, C.D. (or A.B.), to be my lawful wedded wife (or husband, or spouse)"; or words to that effect.
turn_offs_found.why: Accurate, but this and the next legal quote are long blocks of formal text. Hard going on an iPad without a plain-English line to sum them up.

would_share_with: My daughter, example 6 about the years our hair turns grey, and the large-print card tip
My husband, the line about one Wedded Advisor handling payments, with my question about deposits
My sister, the legal words section, because she'll want to know the celebrant has to say it properly

cta_reaction.quote: Start a conversation through Wedded Concierge, and for more ceremony ideas, read the Wedded Wonderland magazine.
cta_reaction.why: Polite and not pushy. But vows are the couple's job. I'd only enquire once my daughter has picked a place, and I'd want a phone call with a named person about deposits, AUD quotes and looking after my mother.

top_3_changes: Add a one-line plain-English summary under the two legal quotes so they're easier to follow on a phone or iPad.
In the Marrying overseas section, say in one line who checks the legal paperwork and language for an overseas ceremony, only if the business confirms it; otherwise flag.
Next to the microphone tip, note whether the Wedded Advisor arranges sound and seating for older or hard-of-hearing guests, sourced from the business or flagged.

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft
Journey types limited to gained_trust, lost_trust, confused, bored, excited, objection
Stayed in character as Margaret (funding parent): read top to bottom on iPad, focused on accountability, deposits, older guests and a phone call
No invented brand facts; deposits, AUD fees, overseas paperwork, guest accessibility and first contact placed in unanswered_questions
VERIFY markers and HTML comments (fact tags, image slots) ignored

open_questions.question: Can the editor add a plain-English summary line after the section 45(2) and 46(1) quotes? Also, can the business confirm who handles legal paperwork for overseas ceremonies and whether the Advisor arranges sound and seating for older guests? If not, flag rather than fill.

assumptions: Margaret arrived via a link from her daughter, reading on an iPad, as a parent contributing about half.
Relevance and enquiry are low because vow wording is the couple's decision, not hers; the careful legal section and practical delivery tips lift trust.
Full article read top to bottom; vow examples skimmed for tone rather than studied.
